content: Furosemide, commonly referred to as a water pill, is prescribed to alleviate swelling and fluid retention caused by conditions such as heart or liver disease. This medication works by prompting the kidneys to excrete excess water and salt into the urine. In some cases, furosemide may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Furosemide is available in tablet and liquid forms, which are taken orally. It is typically administered once daily in the morning or twice daily, in the morning and afternoon. Follow the instructions on your prescription label meticulously, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take furosemide exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. Before starting furosemide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to furosemide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications.g., prednisone), digoxin (Lanoxin), indomethacin (Indocin), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), diabetes medications, probenecid (Benemid), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while taking furosemide. If you become pregnant while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking furosemide. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations, which may include a low-sodium or low-salt diet, potassium supplements, and increased consumption of potassium-rich foods such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice. Your doctor may also suggest a daily exercise regimen. If you miss a dose of furosemide, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination is a common side effect of furosemide and may persist for up to six hours after a dose. This effect typically diminishes after a few weeks of use. Notify your doctor if any of the following minor side effects are severe or persistent: muscle cramps, weakness, dizziness, confusion, thirst, upset stomach, vomiting, blurred vision, headache, restlessness, or constipation. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor if you experience fever, sore throat, ringing in the ears, unusual bleeding or bruising, hearing loss, severe rash with peeling skin, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or rapid and excessive weight loss. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store furosemide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Discard any unused liquid furosemide after 60 days, as well as any expired or unnecessary medication. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Furosemide is sold under the brand name Lasix®.
